records.title: Frost Armor: keeping your stacks is the survival plan
records.summary: Frost Armor reduces the damage you take. Bungie’s June update listed roughly 35% protection at five stacks in PvE, rising to 50% at seven stacks with Whisper of Rime.
records.text:
Frost Armor reduces the damage you take. Bungie’s June update listed roughly 35% protection at five stacks in PvE, rising to 50% at seven stacks with Whisper of Rime.

Why it matters
For a tank build, uptime matters as much as the highest number. Under those published values, a hit that would deal 100 damage would deal about 65 at five stacks, or 50 at seven, before any other effects. That example is arithmetic from the patch values, not a new gameplay measurement. Bungie also described stacks wearing off one at a time, giving you a chance to refresh the buff before losing all its protection.

How to use it
1. Choose a setup with a reliable way to gain Frost Armor, and watch its stack counter during a fight.
2. If your subclass offers Whisper of Rime, compare its higher stack cap with the fragment you would give up.
3. Build and refresh your stacks before exposing yourself to sustained enemy fire; retreat when the protection starts dropping.

What to watch for
These are published PvE values. They do not establish PvP protection, and adding a second defensive effect does not mean you can simply add its percentage to Frost Armor.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: No Backup Plans: use kills to keep defensive buffs going
records.summary: Bungie changed No Backup Plans so shotgun or melee final blows extend defensive buffs you already have and start health regeneration.
records.text:
Bungie changed No Backup Plans so shotgun or melee final blows extend defensive buffs you already have and start health regeneration.

Why it matters
The interesting part is maintaining a buff that normally expires. The patch names Void Overshield, Restoration, Amplified, Frost Armor and Woven Mail. That makes this a Titan build idea centred on creating protection first, then sustaining it through close-range kills. It is especially relevant if you enjoy staying in the fight rather than stopping to rebuild your defences.

How to use it
1. Choose a separate, reliable source of the defensive buff you want to maintain.
2. Activate that buff before engaging a group.
3. Use shotgun or melee final blows to test how long you can keep it active, while watching the timer and your health.

What to watch for
No Backup Plans no longer grants a fresh Void Overshield by itself under this change. Do not build the loop around receiving an overshield from nothing. Extension duration and endgame uptime still need a live check.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Smoke Jumper: check the bonus before calling it a tank build
records.summary: Bungie’s June update reduced the maximum protection from the two-piece Smoke Jumper bonus from 50% to 40% in PvE.
records.text:
Bungie’s June update reduced the maximum protection from the two-piece Smoke Jumper bonus from 50% to 40% in PvE.

Why it matters
This matters when an old build guide promises a level of protection the set no longer provides under that patch. The word “maximum” also matters: wearing two pieces does not prove that the full bonus is active throughout a fight. Your build needs to satisfy the set’s trigger and maintain it.

How to use it
1. Read the set bonus on the two armor pieces you intend to wear.
2. Check when its protection activates and when it falls away.
3. Compare that real uptime with the stats and other armor bonuses you give up.

What to watch for
The patch’s maximum is not an always-on 40% reduction. This record does not establish a PvP value or how the bonus combines with other protection.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Controlled Burst + Charge Time masterwork: check the perk is working
records.summary: Bungie’s known-issues record reports that Controlled Burst can fail on fusion rifles with a Charge Time masterwork.
records.text:
Bungie’s known-issues record reports that Controlled Burst can fail on fusion rifles with a Charge Time masterwork.

Why it matters
A roll can look excellent on paper and still fail to deliver its advertised perk. If your fusion has this combination, test whether Controlled Burst actually activates before relying on it for a boss phase. A rating based on perk names cannot detect the practical loss of a perk that is not working.

How to use it
1. Open your fusion and check both its selected trait and masterwork.
2. If it has this combination, test a full burst against a suitable target and watch for the perk activating.
3. Compare it with another copy or another fusion before committing it to your damage loadout.

What to watch for
This is an acknowledged issue in the source we reviewed, not a fresh test of your weapon. Check Bungie’s latest issue status before assuming your copy is affected or fixed.

Source & status
Bungie known-issues page reviewed 2 November 2026. Your individual weapon has not been retested.

records.title: The same perk twice does not automatically mean double the benefit
records.summary: Bungie has acknowledged weapons dropping with duplicate perks in both trait columns. The drop can be real without proving the perk stacks twice.
records.text:
Bungie has acknowledged weapons dropping with duplicate perks in both trait columns. The drop can be real without proving the perk stacks twice.

Why it matters
This is worth investigating if you own an unusual roll, but the useful question is whether both copies actually affect the weapon. Two identical icons are not enough to promise twice the damage, ability energy or duration. Keep an unusual copy for comparison rather than judging it only from its appearance.

How to use it
1. Inspect the selected perks in both trait columns.
2. Compare the weapon’s actual buff, damage or refund with a normal copy under the same conditions.
3. Keep the unusual roll while you establish what it does; do not treat it as a confirmed exploit build.

What to watch for
Bungie acknowledged the duplicate drops. Functional double-stacking remains a separate question for each perk.

Source & status
Bungie known-issues page reviewed 2 November 2026. Duplicate drops are acknowledged; extra perk benefits are not established.

records.title: Mantle of Battle Harmony: check your surge with a Solar Super
records.summary: Bungie’s known-issues record says Mantle of Battle Harmony’s weapon surge can stop applying when a Solar Super is equipped.
records.text:
Bungie’s known-issues record says Mantle of Battle Harmony’s weapon surge can stop applying when a Solar Super is equipped.

Why it matters
If a Warlock build depends on the Exotic’s weapon bonus, this can break the central reason for using it. A useful check is whether the expected surge appears with your actual Super selection, rather than assuming every elemental setup behaves the same way.

How to use it
1. Equip the Super and weapon you intend to use.
2. Trigger the Exotic’s normal weapon-bonus condition and check the displayed buff.
3. If the bonus is absent, compare another setup before using that loadout for a difficult encounter.

What to watch for
The issue status needs checking against the current game. No replacement damage multiplier or PvP time-to-kill is established here.

Source & status
Bungie known-issues page reviewed 2 November 2026. Forge has not reproduced the issue on your loadout.

records.title: Argent Blade: make sure Armor Charge is actually arriving
records.summary: Bungie’s issue list reports that Argent Blade can fail to grant Armor Charge when it is your only equipped charge-generating perk.
records.text:
Bungie’s issue list reports that Argent Blade can fail to grant Armor Charge when it is your only equipped charge-generating perk.

Why it matters
A sword loop can feel weaker than expected if the Armor Charge it depends on never appears. Before assuming your damage or ability mods are being fed, watch the Armor Charge indicator after the trigger that should generate it.

How to use it
1. Check that Argent Blade is available and legal in the activity you are entering.
2. Trigger it and watch whether Armor Charge is added.
3. If it is not, test a separate, legal Armor Charge source so you can identify which part of the loop is failing.

What to watch for
This does not promise that adding any second perk fixes it. Confirm the source and resulting charge in-game. Artifact effects cannot be assumed active in every PvP playlist.

Source & status
Bungie known-issues page reviewed 2 November 2026. Current activity and Artifact availability need checking.

records.title: A free Grapple is not a free Grenade Kickstart refund
records.summary: Bungie fixed Grenade Kickstart activating from free Grapples supplied by a Grapple Tangle or the Grappler modifier.
records.text:
Bungie fixed Grenade Kickstart activating from free Grapples supplied by a Grapple Tangle or the Grappler modifier.

Why it matters
This is an important limit on an “unlimited abilities” loop. A Grapple that costs no grenade energy should not be counted as spending a grenade and earning a Kickstart refund under this correction. Otherwise a build planner can promise more grenade energy than the game actually gives you.

How to use it
1. Separate your paid Grapples from free Grapples when testing the loop.
2. Watch grenade energy after each type rather than combining them into one average.
3. Choose another supported refund source if the build relies on getting energy from every free Grapple.

What to watch for
The patch establishes the free-Grapple exception. It does not establish your exact grenade recharge time or every other refund interaction.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Lament + Stronghold: a Heavy-sword survival idea to test
records.summary: The research points to Lament for a Titan sword setup because it is a Heavy sword. Bungie limited Stronghold’s infinite guard to Heavy swords.
records.text:
The research points to Lament for a Titan sword setup because it is a Heavy sword. Bungie limited Stronghold’s infinite guard to Heavy swords.

Why it matters
That distinction matters if you are copying a sword build: you cannot assume a Special-ammo sword receives the same guard behaviour. The source also records Lament’s charged light attacks being fixed to trigger sword-based Artifact perks, with later changes partly restoring its final-combo damage and self-healing. Together these are reasons to investigate the combination, not proof of an invincible loadout.

How to use it
1. Use the Heavy sword Lament with Stronghold when testing this particular guard interaction.
2. Test guarding and Lament’s attack/healing sequence separately, then combine them.
3. Add an available sword Artifact perk only after checking that Lament’s charged attacks actually trigger it in your activity.

What to watch for
Exact protection, healing uptime and current Artifact choices are not established by these patch notes. This is a build direction, not a completed “unkillable” build.

Source & status
Based on Bungie’s 24 February and 9 June 2026 changes. The combined loop has not been retested in the current patch.

records.title: Trinity Ghoul: chain kills can matter for your next ammo drop
records.summary: Bungie fixed Lightning Rod chain kills failing to grant ammo progress.
records.text:
Bungie fixed Lightning Rod chain kills failing to grant ammo progress.

Why it matters
Trinity Ghoul’s value is not only how quickly it clears a group. If those chain kills contribute to ammo progress as described, that clear can also help prepare your Special or Heavy economy for what comes next. This is a reason to compare the whole encounter, not just one arrow’s damage.

How to use it
1. Use Lightning Rod to clear a comparable group of enemies.
2. Track ammo progress or subsequent ammo availability across several repeatable groups.
3. Compare that result with ordinary bow kills before deciding whether the weapon improves your loadout’s ammo economy.

What to watch for
The patch does not give an exact amount of ammo progress or promise the same kill credit for every Exotic, Artifact perk or PvP mode.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Vortex Ergo Sum: old six-ammo heavy-attack advice can mislead you
records.summary: Bungie corrected Ergo Sum’s Vortex heavy attack spending six ammo instead of four.
records.text:
Bungie corrected Ergo Sum’s Vortex heavy attack spending six ammo instead of four.

Why it matters
An old rotation built around the bug can understate how many heavy attacks your reserve supports after the fix. The practical benefit is ammo efficiency for that particular attack, not an automatic increase to every hit’s damage. It also does not turn a Special sword into a Heavy sword for armor interactions.

How to use it
1. Confirm your Ergo Sum uses the Vortex frame.
2. Watch the ammo counter before and after its heavy attack.
3. Plan your attack sequence around the cost your copy actually spends, rather than an old clip showing the six-ammo bug.

What to watch for
This correction concerns Vortex heavy-attack cost. It does not establish boss damage per second or a way to generate sword ammo in PvP.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-23. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.summary: Bungie fixed the non-enhanced version of Forge’s Kin failing to receive its increased benefits when multiple Black Armory weapons were equipped.
records.text:
Bungie fixed the non-enhanced version of Forge’s Kin failing to receive its increased benefits when multiple Black Armory weapons were equipped.

Why it matters
The interaction to investigate is the equipment combination. If you are evaluating the trait with only one relevant weapon equipped, you are not testing the extra benefit described in the correction. This is a potential reason to compare a matching set of weapons with your usual mixed loadout.

How to use it
1. Check whether your selected weapon has the non-enhanced Forge’s Kin trait.
2. Compare its behaviour with one relevant Black Armory weapon equipped, then with multiple relevant weapons.
3. Decide whether the observed benefit is worth changing the rest of your loadout.

What to watch for
The source does not give an exact bonus and does not establish the enhanced version’s behaviour. Specific current weapon versions and available rolls still need checking.

Source & status

records.title: Pyrogale: the explosion buff is not 10% more damage to the whole Super
records.summary: Bungie described a 10% increase to the Super Cyclone’s explosion component and roughly 40% better tracking for Pyrogale Gauntlets.
records.text:
Bungie described a 10% increase to the Super Cyclone’s explosion component and roughly 40% better tracking for Pyrogale Gauntlets.

Why it matters
The distinction matters when comparing boss damage. Better tracking may help the effect connect, but the published 10% change applies to its explosion component. Applying that increase to all ticks, Scorch and every other part of the Super would exaggerate the benefit.

How to use it
1. Compare the explosion hit separately from the rest of the Super’s damage.
2. Use a repeatable target so missed hits do not masquerade as a damage change.
3. For a moving target, judge how reliably the cyclone connects as well as its largest damage number.

What to watch for
The patch numbers do not establish a total boss damage increase or the same effects against Guardians.

Source & status

records.summary: Bungie described a delayed Solar explosion and Solar shrapnel when most Blade Barrage knives land while using Shards of Galanor.
records.text:
Bungie described a delayed Solar explosion and Solar shrapnel when most Blade Barrage knives land while using Shards of Galanor.

Why it matters
That makes hit consistency important to the Exotic’s payoff. A throw that scatters knives away from the target may not be comparable with one that lands the required hits. Look at the delayed follow-up as well as the first wave of knife damage.

How to use it
1. Choose a target and position where your Blade Barrage knives can connect consistently.
2. Watch for the delayed explosion and shrapnel after the knives land.
3. Compare complete damage sequences rather than judging only the first damage numbers.

What to watch for
The source does not give the exact knife threshold or a verified boss damage total. PvP behaviour must be checked separately.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Touch of Thunder: tracking can matter more than a paper damage number
records.summary: Bungie increased the Storm Grenade’s duration by half a second and its maximum tracking speed against PvE enemies by 38%, while increasing the time it takes to reach that speed by 25%.
records.text:
Bungie increased the Storm Grenade’s duration by half a second and its maximum tracking speed against PvE enemies by 38%, while increasing the time it takes to reach that speed by 25%.

Why it matters
The trade-off is that a higher eventual tracking speed does not mean instant acceleration. For moving enemies, what matters is how many damage ticks actually connect during the grenade’s lifetime. The extra duration and tracking changes are reasons to compare real hit consistency rather than assume a flat damage multiplier.

How to use it
1. Use Storm Grenade with Touch of Thunder for this comparison.
2. Test it against a repeatably moving PvE target.
3. Count connected ticks and the complete damage sequence, keeping your other build choices fixed.

What to watch for
The tracking figures are stated for combatants. They do not establish faster tracking against Guardians or a PvP kill time.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Deadshot’s energy nerf does not mean 40% less shot damage
records.summary: Bungie reduced the Super energy gained from player kills during Golden Gun: Deadshot by 40%.
records.text:
Bungie reduced the Super energy gained from player kills during Golden Gun: Deadshot by 40%.

Why it matters
This changes the energy return from a kill, not the damage of a Golden Gun shot. If you are comparing old Crucible clips, a chain of kills may sustain the Super differently after this change even when an individual shot still behaves as expected.

How to use it
1. Keep the same Super variant when comparing clips or tests.
2. Watch the Super meter after a player kill rather than treating shot damage as the changed value.
3. Plan follow-up engagements around the energy that remains, not an older kill-chain demonstration.

What to watch for
This is not a 40% reduction to the entire Super duration, all recharge sources or every shot’s damage.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Skull of Dire Ahamkara: watch for the Nova Lance follow-up
records.summary: Bungie described a short Nova Lance opportunity after casting Nova Bomb with Skull of Dire Ahamkara. Destroying a Cataclysm Nova Bomb with Nova Lance creates a Nova Vortex alongside the seekers.
records.text:
Bungie described a short Nova Lance opportunity after casting Nova Bomb with Skull of Dire Ahamkara. Destroying a Cataclysm Nova Bomb with Nova Lance creates a Nova Vortex alongside the seekers.

Why it matters
This is an interaction to test as a sequence, not just a passive damage bonus. Its value depends on landing the follow-up within the window and on what the Vortex and seekers actually hit. Time spent on that follow-up also needs comparing with returning to your weapons.

How to use it
1. Use Skull of Dire Ahamkara with the relevant Nova Bomb setup.
2. After casting, check for the Nova Lance follow-up window and test the described Cataclysm interaction.
3. Compare the full sequence with a normal cast followed immediately by weapon fire.

What to watch for
The source does not give the window length or Nova Lance damage. This is a testing idea, not a verified highest-damage boss rotation.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Multiple ability charges: check what you actually start a match with
records.summary: Bungie’s June patch states that multi-charge abilities start a PvP match with one charge.
records.text:
Bungie’s June patch states that multi-charge abilities start a PvP match with one charge.

Why it matters
A build can have room for multiple charges without giving you all of them at the opening spawn. This matters if your first engagement assumes two immediate uses. Build the opening plan around the charge that is actually available, then assess later recharges separately.

How to use it
1. Enter the intended PvP mode and check the ability counter at match start.
2. Plan the opening engagement around that starting count.
3. Measure later recharge behaviour separately from the opening restriction.

What to watch for
The starting-charge rule does not give a recharge time or remove the ability’s later capacity for more charges. Check mode-specific rules before relying on Artifact effects.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Cusp Sempiternal: an old Withering Gaze aiming bug was fixed
records.summary: Bungie fixed Cusp Sempiternal’s Withering Gaze failing to weaken unless you were still aiming when the projectile reached its target.
records.text:
Bungie fixed Cusp Sempiternal’s Withering Gaze failing to weaken unless you were still aiming when the projectile reached its target.

Why it matters
That distinction matters for a shoot-then-swap playstyle. The old impact-time aiming requirement was a bug, so it should not be copied into a guide as the intended trigger. You still need to satisfy the perk’s actual activation condition before firing.

How to use it
1. Read Withering Gaze’s activation requirement on your copy.
2. Activate it, fire, then compare staying aimed with your normal weapon swap.
3. Watch for weakening on the same PvE target before adopting the swap sequence.

What to watch for
The correction does not remove the perk’s normal trigger. It also does not establish a damage increase or time-to-kill against Guardians.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.
